# Phase 0 Part 6: Complete the native mobile document foundation

Logistics now has native Home, Files, Documents and Settings navigation on iOS
and Android, destination-local Back routes, independent text/Markdown editors,
ordinary draft recovery and adaptive open-list/editor panes. This release builds
on the already pushed foundation and completes its close and restoration flows.

- **Part 1:** Dirty document Close offers Save, Keep draft, Discard and Cancel.
  Failed saves keep the session open; Discard preserves external file changes.
- **Part 2:** Edit/Preview mode follows each document. Preview callbacks target
  their original session and cannot reopen a closed document.
- **Part 3:** Unavailable restored documents offer Retry/Remove while preserving
  the current editor and every existing source/recovery file.
- **Part 4:** Record native evidence and prepare the numbered release notes.
- **Part 5:** Use Material-themed Android bars so inactive destinations remain
  visible; verify icon and label contrast in native tests.
- **Part 6:** Verify normal launchers and submit the validated foundation.

The included checkpoint also provides library sessions, Settings connection
management and one-time unencrypted remote folder pulls with visible progress.
Repeatable sync, broader reader/Files refinement, private-session expansion and
independent windows remain later phases.

Validation: 45 mobile regression tests, 32 document/workspace/reader/privacy
checks, and all 18 native UI cases on both iPhone Duo (iOS 27.1 simulator) and
Android 15. Normal and test-mode native builds are checked separately. Local
native reports retain the exact staged fingerprint and are labeled development
evidence; automated release gates still control asset publication.

Physical provider permissions, real fold gestures, iOS 15 compatibility,
accessibility combinations and BOOX/E Ink behavior remain unverified device gates.
